description:
FILED s433 (Fable review probe of s432; PRE-EXISTING on bc02000 and before).

A plain call to a NEVER-declared sub reaches no AUTOLOAD and dies with SBCL's raw undefined-function:

    our $AUTOLOAD; sub AUTOLOAD { "A($AUTOLOAD)" }   print nope(1), "\n";
        perl: A(main::nope)         PCL: Unhandled undefined-function (SBCL backtrace, rc != 0)
    print nope(1), "\n";
        perl: dies "Undefined subroutine &main::nope called at F line 1."
        PCL: the same SBCL error; inside eval {} $@ = "The function main::pl-nope is undefined. at (eval 0) line 0."
    sub nope; <the same two>     <- RIGHT since s432 (#456 half (a)): the stub runs %p-call-of-undefined-sub

The emission is a direct `(pl-nope 1)`; nothing turns SBCL's condition into perl's order.  s432's `%p-call-of-undefined-sub` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp) IS that order -- own-package AUTOLOAD with $AUTOLOAD set, no @ISA walk, else perl's die.  It is the ONE mechanism for "a plain call reached no body"; route the never-declared path through it (rule 11).

TWO CANDIDATE ROUTES, decide by measurement:
  (1) an `undefined-function` handler at the program's dynamic extent -- SBCL offers a `use-value` restart: hand it `(lambda (&rest a) (%p-call-of-undefined-sub sym a))`.  First find WHERE that extent is established (runpcl / the installed bin wrapper / `p-eval-block` for the eval {} case / the sweep's p-load-with-recovery) -- the handler must be in every one of them or it is a second drifting runner axis.
  (2) emit `(p-declare-sub NAME)` for every called-but-undeclared name (the stub route): every such call then reaches the stub, which already does the right thing.  Emission change -> generation bump + four-population A/B; CHECK that p-import / p-sub clear the :stub mark (they set :defined -- verify for the Exporter path, since a `use Foo; foo()` call is undeclared at transpile and resolved by import at load).

BAR: the rows above with and without eval {}; `sort nonexistent LIST` (already right via p-get-coderef -- must stay); a METHOD call unaffected (the @ISA walk is the method rule); a never-declared call in a package WITH an AUTOLOAD and one WITHOUT; full sweep (runtime) + the A/B if route (2).  Guard rows in Pl/t/decl-ordering-02.t beside the s432 ones.

Ruling: docs/fable-answers-s433.md Â§B.1 / Â§C.1.  Queue: plan-post-s433 Q7.


DONE s441c (agent C, Opus; merged by Fable s440 as f6faeb0). NEITHER listed route -- both measured and rejected (the record is the runtime comment above %p-pcl-sub-symbol-p in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp): (1) the program's dynamic extent is NOT centralised (runpcl, pl2cl, install-pcl's wrapper, p-load-with-recovery, ~40 Pl/t files each --load their own file) and a global SBCL handler cluster does not survive to the next toplevel form (probed); SBCL has no undefined-function hook. (2) 8-37 undeclared call names per corpus file (ref.t 14, sort.t 37, bless.t 8) => an emission diff in every file of every population, `exists &nope` becomes 1 where perl says 0 (probed), and s432's stub-vs-later-definition interaction multiplies. CHOSEN: encapsulate sb-kernel::restart-undefined (%p-install-undefined-sub-dispatch, once at load, idempotent, announces on stderr if the internal disappears) so the handler is INNERMOST at signal time -- it runs before p-eval-block's handler-case, which route (1) never could, and eval {} sees the AUTOLOAD value. No emission change, no runner change, no generation bump, zero cost until an undefined function is called. It DECLINES for anything that is not a `pl-...` symbol in a :pcl-using package (probed: a missing p-... builtin, a pl- name in a non-PCL package, a plain CL name all keep their loud CL error). p-backslash-sub's "not declared at all" branch was a SECOND COPY that disagreed on five points -- routed through the one function, with an fboundp re-check so late binding still wins; %p-sub-perl-name's symbol test extracted as %p-sub-bare-name and shared. Guard: 5 rows in Pl/t/decl-ordering-02.t (26 total), 4 of which fail on a base tree. docs/ir-spec.md sec. 5.1 records the rule. DO NOT RETRY the stub-emission or the extent-handler routes. Found while probing: `sort NAME LIST` emits a THIRD copy of the AUTOLOAD dispatch (Pl/ExprToCL.pm ~3617) whose no-AUTOLOAD arm returns nil -- `sort nonexistent LIST` was SILENT WRONG, not "already right"; the wrapper is now dead code -- #501.
